invalid_if: Delivery availability is not disclosed before the order is placed
name: Scope of the Shipping and Delivery Policy
title: Scope
text:
This Policy is published by {{company_name}} and takes effect from {{effective_date}} (the "Effective Date"). It sets out how {{company_name}} ships and delivers orders placed on {{website_url}}, and forms part of the information Rule 4 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 requires an e-commerce entity to display.
(a) This Policy applies to {{goods_or_services_description}}.
(b) {{company_name}} delivers to the areas stated on the platform, and the platform states before an order is placed whether delivery to the consumer's address is available.
(c) Nothing in this Policy limits a right the consumer has under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 or any other law.
(d) {{company_name}} may amend this Policy, and an amendment takes effect when it is published. An order placed before an amendment is governed by the Policy in force when the order was placed.

legal_basis.note: Accurate information relating to delivery and shipment must be displayed

source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020; Consumer Protection Act, 2019
authoring_note:
Limb (b) requires serviceability to be disclosed pre-order, since taking payment for an undeliverable address is a deficiency in service from the outset.

The Effective Date and the amendment terms live in THIS clause, not in the adoption block. A SIGNATURE_BLOCK clause has its text generated by signatureResolver, so anything authored there is discarded -- which is how the Effective Date went missing from the first draft of this policy.
